title: add support for projects having the kainbain docs in a seperate repo large projects may end up bloated with the project kainbain tasks/docs or we may be working on a repo with others who are non kainbain users. There may be reasons we dont want kainbain specific docs in the repo (maybe we just dont want to reveal the information publicly) therefore as an advance option we should be able to give a remote repo that is used to store kainbain specific information. This will need to be loaded onto runners adjacent to the main project repo, with synced task branches in order to keep things as similar to normal operations as possible . In UI configuration this should be allowed from the default when you import/create a new project (especially on an import)  Goal is allow people to use this without having their full team go in on it  (or so I can stealth use kainbain at work )
goal:
# add support for projects having the kainbain docs in a seperate repo

large projects may end up bloated with the project kainbain tasks/docs or we may be working on a repo with others who are non kainbain users. There may be reasons we dont want kainbain specific docs in the repo (maybe we just dont want to reveal the information publicly)

therefore as an advance option we should be able to give a remote repo that is used to store kainbain specific information. This will need to be loaded onto runners adjacent to the main project repo, with synced task branches in order to keep things as similar to normal operations as possible .

In UI configuration this should be allowed from the default when you import/create a new project (especially on an import) 


Goal is allow people to use this without having their full team go in on it  (or so I can stealth use kainbain at work )

## Human Correction / Feedback
Cant see settings in the Ui
body:
# add support for projects having the kainbain docs in a seperate repo

large projects may end up bloated with the project kainbain tasks/docs or we may be working on a repo with others who are non kainbain users. There may be reasons we dont want kainbain specific docs in the repo (maybe we just dont want to reveal the information publicly)

therefore as an advance option we should be able to give a remote repo that is used to store kainbain specific information. This will need to be loaded onto runners adjacent to the main project repo, with synced task branches in order to keep things as similar to normal operations as possible .

In UI configuration this should be allowed from the default when you import/create a new project (especially on an import) 


Goal is allow people to use this without having their full team go in on it  (or so I can stealth use kainbain at work )

Cant see settings in the Ui

{"content":"# Fix verification — "Cant see settings in the Ui" (stage 4, 2026-11-20)

## Root cause (confirmed by bundle forensics this attempt)

The instance the human checks (`http://192.168.1.206:3100`, bundle
`/assets/index-Ci5jdoJ7.js`, fetched live this attempt) runs a build from
before this branch's visibility fixes:

- It contains the bare label `Advanced options` ×2 (Create + Adopt) with the
  body rendered only under `k && (<div …>` — i.e. **closed by default**, no
  naming of the option — and **zero** occurrences of
  `Advanced options: separate docs repo` (grep count 0).
- It does contain the Settings → Files & Repos docs-repo input, but the
  Create/Import path — the one the task text calls "allowed from the
  default" — shows no trace of the setting until the user guesses to expand
  a generic "Advanced options".

Current branch source fixes all three defects (all verified in source this
attempt, not just by tests):

- `frontend/src/components/layout/Header.jsx:316,327` —
  `useState(true)` for both `createAdvancedOpen`/`adoptAdvancedOpen`:
  Advanced is **expanded by default**; the toggle is named
  "Advanced options: separate docs repo" (`Header.jsx:849,997`) so it stays
  findable even if collapsed.
- `Header.jsx:764,785,895,916` — dialog `max-h-[90vh]` + pinned header +
  scrolling form (the `SystemGuideModal` pattern): the docs field and the
  Create/Add buttons stay reachable on short viewports.
- `frontend/src/components/settings/PathsAndReposSection.jsx:202` — bordered
  "📚 Separate Docs Repository" block (heading + Enabled/Disabled status +
  URL + local-path fields) in Settings → Files & Repos; the Project tab
  carries the `Separate Docs Repository: On/Off` summary row with a
  "Manage in Files & Repos" jump (`ProjectBasicsSection.jsx:349`); the
  settings search index covers `separate/docs/repo/private/stealth/remote`
  (`projectSettingsSearch.js:174,181`).

No further source change was needed: the defect was deployment age, not
code. This stage therefore re-proves visibility from current source and
confirms the branch is merge-ready; the setting becomes visible in
`192.168.1.206:3100` when the engine merges this branch and runs
`deploy.sh --prod` (the backend host is a different machine,
`192.168.1.206` ≠ this runner's `192.168.1.172`, so there is no
in-worktree way to push it there).

## This attempt's evidence (all observed, not assumed)

- Frontend tests (touched area): `npx vitest run Header / ProjectSettings /
  PathsAndReposSection / ProjectBasicsSection / projectSettingsSearch` —
  **159/159 pass**.
- Fresh production bundle: `npx vite build` green (4.35s); the new
  `frontend/dist` bundle contains `Advanced options: separate docs repo`,
  `Separate Docs Repository URL`, `Docs Repo Local Path`,
  `Separate Docs Repository:`, `Configure in Files & Repos`, and
  `max-h-[90vh]` (each ≥1 file in `dist/assets/`). `frontend/dist` is
  gitignored — deploy rebuilds it.
- Live UI proof from THIS branch (vite dev serving branch source + stub API
  with a `docsRepo`-enabled project, headless Chromium @1280×720 —
  realistic laptop viewport, script at `/tmp/verify-docsrepo-ui.mjs`):
  **11/11 DOM assertions pass**, including "Create dialog renders the docs
  URL field without clicking the toggle" and "field inside the 720px
  viewport" (y=455).
- Screenshots (PNG magic + `file` verified, `check:binaries` and
  `check:proof-hygiene` green):
  - `stage4-proof-1-create-720.png` — Create dialog, Advanced open, docs
    URL field + explainer visible, buttons reachable.
  - `stage4-proof-2-adopt-720-scrolled.png` — Add Existing dialog,

1|# PR Review — Separate docs repo per project (task 7f6220c3)
2|
3|Reviewer stage: PR review. Verdict: **PASS** (details at the bottom).
4|Scope of review: full `git diff main` (62 files, +9453/−99), previous stage reports, and live verification runs. No source files were modified in this stage; only this report and three screenshots under this task's docs folder were added.
5|
6|## 1. Does it achieve the goal?
7|
8|Yes. A project can now keep ALL KainBain information (task docs, plans, reports, and the `.kainbain/` state incl. `project.json`) in a separate private git repo:
9|
10|- **Opt-in config surface**: `docsRepo: { url, localPath?, branchMode: "synced" }` on the project record, accepted by `POST /projects`, `POST /projects/register`, and `PATCH /projects/:id` (`api/routes/projects.js`). In the UI it appears under a collapsed **Advanced options** disclosure on both the New Project and Add Existing Project dialogs (`frontend/src/components/layout/Header.jsx` + new `DocsRepoFields.jsx`), and in Project Settings → Files & Repositories (`PathsAndReposSection.jsx`, `ProjectSettingsForm.jsx`) for enable/disable later. Matches survey q2 (Advanced section) and the task text ("allowed from the default when you import/create").
11|- **Stealth (q5)**: with `docsRepo` set, nothing KainBain-related is written into the main repo — `createProject` skips the `.gitignore` write and the docs symlink (`api/projectStore.js:978,1020`), `ensureDocsLink` returns `external-docs` and never touches `<cwd>/docs` (`api/projectStore.js:1523`), `_migrateDocsLink` is skipped (`api/projectStore.js:2082`), and the pointer map (`docs-repo-pointers.json`) lives engine-globally next to the projects registry, never in the main repo (`api/project/docsRepoPointer.js`). Guards: `assertDocsRepoSeparateFromMain` 400s when `localPath` is inside the main repo or `url` equals the main remote; `_assertDocsRepoUnclaimed` 409s when another project claims the same URL/path (q7: one per project). All covered by tests in `api/routes/projects.docsRepo.test.js` (incl. "keeps the main repo clean" and "writes nothing KainBain into it").
12|- **Single seam**: `resolveKainbainHome(cwd, project)` (`api/project/resolveKainbainHome.js`) maps docs/state resolution onto `docsRepo.localPath` when set, else `cwd`. `resolveDocsPath`, `resolveKainbainDir` and everything derived from them (`resolveTasksDir`, `resolveTaskDocsDir`, `resolveSessionsDir`, `resolveWorktreesDir`, `resolveQuarantineDir`, `resolveProjectConfigPath`, `reportRelPath`) chain through it. `promptCuration.js` was fixed to route through `resolveTaskDocsDir` instead of hand-building `<cwd>/docs/...`. Legacy projects (no `docsRepo`) are byte-identical — proven by `api/docsRepoResolution.test.js`.
13|- **Runners (the core ask)**: `prepareWorkdir` grows `docsRepoUrl`/`docsLocalPath` and prepares a paired docs worktree `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>-docs` on the SAME `kb/<taskId>` branch from its own mirror (clone mode) or adopted checkout (`runner/project.js`). The pair counts as one `WORKTREE_CAP` slot; `listOrphanWorkdirs` hides the `-docs` twin and eviction/reap treat the pair atomically. The claim payload carries the redacted `docsRepoUrl` (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`), so remote runners can clone both. `shouldSyncTaskDocs` skips the primary→worktree docs copy when the docs worktree exists (docs already live there via git); `collectTaskFiles` and `KAINBAIN_TASK_DOCS` read from the docs worktree; `applyBackendPrompt` retargets backend-curated docs paths to the runner's docs worktree (docs-home rewrite first, to avoid the `<cwd>-kainbain-docs` prefix trap); `commitAndPush` commits+pushes the docs worktree FIRST and labels failures `docs repo (...)` before any code push (`runner/gitOps.js`). Real-git integration tests cover clone mode, adopt mode, same-URL refusal, docs-first push order, and docs-failure-aborts-code-push (`runner/project.docsRepo.test.js`).
14|- **Auth (q3)**: same login as the main repo (ambient git credentials); stored URL is credential-redacted at write and re-redacted on read/exposure (`normalizeDocsRepoSettings`, `docsRepoUrlFor`, `assertValidDocsRepoForWrite`). Matches the survey answer; no new secret surface.
15|
16|## 2. Did it follow the plan?
17|
18|Mostly yes. Phase 1's "make change easy" seam (`resolveKainbainHome`) landed exactly as designed (D1), the validation scaffolding (D4) is strict-on-write/tolerant-on-read with `INVALID_DOCS_REPO_*` codes like the existing docsDirName pattern, and the runner seam prep (D5) exists (`docsWorkdirFor`, `shouldSyncTaskDocs`). Two documented deviations from the plan/survey, both surfaced in `site-docs/separate-docs-repo.md` as v1 limitations:
19|
20|1. **q4 (existing docs on switch-on)**: survey answer was "Ask me each time"; the implementation leaves old docs in place and only new work goes to the docs repo, with a documented manual move procedure (the plan's ★ recommendation). No per-time prompt exists. Safe and reversible; flagging so the requester can confirm this matches intent.
21|2. **B5 (merge stage)**: docs `kb/*` branches are created/pushed synced but NOT auto-merged at the merge stage in v1 — explicitly documented in the site-docs limitations. Code merge semantics unchanged.
22|
23|## 3. Code standards & best practices
24|
25|- One-function-per-file convention kept: `npm run check:one-function` PASS (860 files).
26|- ESLint on all changed api/frontend files: **0 errors** (only pre-existing warning classes). JSDoc `MARK:` blocks on all new modules; `check:jsdoc-example` and `check-doc-links` pass.
27|- Barrel surface test updated (`api/projectStore.barrel.test.js`) — this was the first CI failure (20261119-145122); now green (60/60 in the new api test files).
28|- Publish gate fixed: `publish.sh` runner gate now lists `runner/project.docsRepo.test.js`, `scripts/run-tests.mjs` includes it, and `tests/publish.test.mjs` regex widened to accept dots in runner test filenames — the second CI failure (20261119-152529); `node --test tests/publish.test.mjs` now 8/8.
29|- No new dependencies; no second git implementation (runner reuses `runGit`/mirror/worktree helpers); no force-push semantics added; recovery/eviction invariants extended to the pair rather than reinvented.
30|
31|## 4. Easy to modify later / tech debt
32|
33|- Compatibility anchor is explicit: absent `docsRepo` = legacy behaviour byte-for-byte, asserted by tests. `branchMode: "synced"` is the only v1 value but the field is stored, so a future "single-branch" mode is additive. One-docs-repo-per-project is enforced with a clear 409 so sharing later is a designed change, not a refactor.
34|- Minor docs gap: `AGENTS-MAP.md` (repo root) line 23 enumerates `api/project/` domains but does not mention the new `docsRepo`/`docsRepoPointer` domains. Not fixable from this docs-only stage; recommend adding one line in a follow-up.
35|- Runner/backend duplication (`resolveRunnerDocsRepoUrl`, `resolveRunnerKainbainHome` mirroring backend) is intentional per the "runner ships standalone" invariant, and documented as such.
36|
37|## 5. Docs updated?
38|
39|- `site-docs/separate-docs-repo.md` — user guide with setup (create/import/settings), how it works, manual move procedure, stealth verification checklist, and v1 limitations. Passes `siteDocs`, `siteDocs.integrity`, `siteDocs.frontendParity`, `siteDocs.deploy`, `agentGuide` tests (55/55).
40|- `CHANGELOG.md` entry added. Task docs (`IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`, `SURVEY.md`) present.
41|
42|## 6. Verification performed in this review (read-only; live app untouched)
43|
44|- New backend tests: 60/60 pass (`project/docsRepo`, `docsRepoPointer`, `assertDocsRepoSeparateFromMain`, `projectStore.barrel`, `docsRepoResolution`, `routes/projects.docsRepo`, `promptCuration.docsDir`).
45|- Related regression suites: 362/362 (`projectStore`, `docsPath`, `kainbainDir`, `work/task*`, `routes/projects*`) and 191/191 (`flow/runnerRoutes`, `promptCuration`).
46|- Full runner gate list from `publish.sh`: 460/460 pass. `tests/publish.test.mjs`: 8/8 pass.
47|- Frontend tests for all changed components: 139/139 pass. ESLint: 0 errors.
48|- UI proof via isolated headless Chromium against a scratch vite dev server on :5299 (serving this branch from source; live :3100 never modified, scratch server stopped afterwards). Screenshots (PNG magic verified):
49|  - `review-create-advanced.png` — New Project dialog, Advanced expanded, "Docs Repository URL (optional)" visible.
50|  - `review-adopt-advanced.png` — Add Existing Project dialog, Advanced expanded, URL + local path fields visible.
51|  - `review-settings-docsrepo.png` — Project Settings → Files & Repos shows "Separate Docs Repository URL (optional)" and "Docs Repository Local Path (optional)".
52|  - Note: the app currently deployed on :3100 runs the older build and does not show the new section — expected, since this branch is not deployed.
53|
54|## Verdict
55|
56|PASS. The feature achieves the stated goal (separate private docs repo, runners get an adjacent checkout with synced `kb/<taskId>` branches, UI option under Advanced on create/import plus settings, main repo stays trace-free with enforced guards), follows the approved plan's seam design, meets the repo's code standards, keeps legacy behaviour byte-identical, and both previous CI failures are fixed and re-verified green. The two deviations (q4 leave-in-place instead of per-time prompt; no automatic docs-branch merge in v1) are documented v1 limitations, not defects.

## Directory ownership and reviewer roles

Roster sourced from `docs/ARCHITECTURE_DOMAINS.md`; role titles only, never individual
names. A PR touching a row needs the matching reviewer; cross-domain changes need every
affected reviewer. Until a volunteer steps up, the domain reviewer for the most-affected
area stands in as **Docs Steward**.

## No-split decisions

- `frontend/src/context/KainBainContext.jsx` (~470 LOC) intentionally stays a single shell composed from focused `use*` hooks in `frontend/src/context/`. No split PR is pending; do not expect one. Satellite hooks: `useBoardSync.js`, `useAccentTheme.js`, `useSelectedTask`, `useViewNavigation` (among others).
- `frontend/src/services/api.js` is a compatibility facade; new requests go in `frontend/src/services/{work,flow,crew,watch,house}/index.js`.
- `api/taskStore.js` and `api/projectStore.js` remain class + singleton facades; pure logic lives in `api/work/` and `api/project/`.

## Barrels that look like code but aren't

- `api/projectStore.js` (~2254 LOC): `ProjectStore` class + singleton wiring only; pure normalizers/utilities live in `api/project/` (WP-3). Registry wiring and persistence stay in the barrel.
- `api/taskStore.js` (~1069 LOC): `TaskStore` class + singleton wiring over `api/{work,flow,watch,house}/index.js` — every method delegates to those subdirs, no business logic lives here. Engine-state composition, owner snapshot, open-queue depth, cwd/link seams, wedge settlement, scheduler kick, and never-throw push seams live as single-purpose modules in `api/work/`. `api/work/index.js` re-exports every cycle-free work module (route registrars stay out — `taskWorkRoutes.js` imports `api/flow/`).
- `api/routes/tasks.js` (~50 LOC): facade registering `taskWorkRoutes` / `taskFlowRoutes` / `taskWatchRoutes`.
- `api/git.js` (~80 LOC): thin re-export barrel over `api/git/*.js` — public surface preserved for caller stability (WP-4). Unit coverage lives in co-located `api/git/*.test.js` (one per command family) plus the 48-export surface contract in `api/git.test.js`.
- `api/flow/stageExecution.js`, `api/flow/stageFailureRouting.js`, `api/flow/taskScheduler.js`: thin re-export barrels over `api/flow/execution/`, `api/flow/routing/` (tables/resolvers/orchestrators), `api/flow/scheduler/` — one module per exported function, public surface byte-identical (WP-5). Loop mechanics import tables/resolvers, never vice versa.
- `shared/toolLogFormat.js` (1 LOC): re-export barrel over `shared/toolLogFormat/*.js` (seams: `stripAnsi`, `truncateAtWord`, `summarizeToolStart`, `summarizeToolResult`, `summarizeUsage`, `summarizePermission`, `summarizePlan`, `summarizeRaw`, and shared helpers). Owner: Watch reviewer.

## `shared/toolLogFormat.js` seam ownership (WP-7)

- `shared/toolLogFormat/index.js` re-exports one subject per file under `shared/toolLogFormat/`.
- Known seams: `stripAnsi`, `truncateAtWord`, `summarizeToolStart`, `summarizeToolResult`, `summarizeUsage`, `summarizePermission`, `summarizePlan`, `summarizeRaw`, plus `toolFamilies`, `constants`, `normalizeBudget`, `parseResultEnvelope`, `pickPrimaryArg`, `readArgValue`, `collapseWhitespace`.

224|/***
225| * MARK: SETTINGS_SEARCH_INDEX
226| * @description Search entries with their tab name filled in from
227| *   `PROJECT_SETTINGS_TABS` (the one place tab names live), so a tab rename
228| *   updates search results instead of leaving a stale copied name behind.
229| *   An entry pointing at an unknown tab keeps a plain fallback name and is
230| *   caught by the agreement test; at runtime the jump handler also ignores
231| *   unknown tabs, so a bad entry can never switch to a blank page.
232| * @example SETTINGS_SEARCH_INDEX.find((e) => e.id === 'git-repo').tabLabel => 'Files & Repos'
233| ***/
234|export const SETTINGS_SEARCH_INDEX = SETTINGS_SEARCH_INDEX_SOURCE_ENTRIES.map((entry) => ({
235|  ...entry,
236|  tabLabel: PROJECT_SETTINGS_TABS.find((tab) => tab.id === entry.tab)?.label ?? 'Project Settings',
237|}));
238|
239|/***
240| * MARK: scoreWord
241| * @description Scores one index entry against a single normalized word: 3 for
242| *   a label prefix match, 2 for a label substring, 1 for a keyword
243| *   substring, 0 for no match. Scores rank `searchSettings` so label hits
244| *   lead. A non-array `keywords` field scores 0 instead of throwing.
245| * @example scoreWord({ label: 'Git Repository URL', keywords: ['git'] }, 'git') => 3
246| * @param {Object} entry - One `SETTINGS_SEARCH_INDEX` entry.
247| * @param {string} word - Lowercase query word.
248| * @returns {number} Match score (0 = no match).
249| ***/
250|const scoreWord = (entry, word) => {
251|  const label = String(entry?.label ?? '').toLowerCase();
252|  if (label.startsWith(word)) return 3;
253|  if (label.includes(word)) return 2;
254|  const keywords = Array.isArray(entry?.keywords) ? entry.keywords : [];
255|  if (keywords.some((keyword) => String(keyword).toLowerCase().includes(word))) return 1;
256|  return 0;
257|};
258|
259|/***
260| * MARK: searchSettings
261| * @description Returns index entries matching a query (case-insensitive).
262| *   Multi-word queries match when EVERY word hits (label substring or
263| *   keyword substring), so "centralised docs folder" finds the docs-link
264| *   setting however the words are ordered. Scores sum the per-word best
265| *   hits, best matches first with index order breaking ties. Blank queries
266| *   and non-matches return an empty array.
267| * @example searchSettings('git') => [{ id: 'git-repo', tab: 'files', … }]
268| * @param {string} query - Raw user input.
269| * @returns {Array<Object>} Matching entries, ranked best-first.
270| ***/
271|export const searchSettings = (query) => {
272|  const normalized = String(query ?? '')
273|    .trim()
274|    .toLowerCase();
275|  if (!normalized) return [];
276|  const words = normalized.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
277|  return SETTINGS_SEARCH_INDEX.map((entry, index) => {
278|    let score = 0;
279|    for (const word of words) {
280|      const wordScore = scoreWord(entry, word);
281|      // One missed word disqualifies the entry (AND semantics).
282|      if (wordScore === 0) return null;
283|      score += wordScore;
284|    }
285|    return { entry, score, index };
286|  })
287|    .filter((hit) => hit !== null)
288|    .sort((first, second) => second.score - first.score || first.index - second.index)
289|    .map((hit) => hit.entry);
290|};
291|
292|/***
293| * MARK: findBestMatch
294| * @description Returns the single best index entry for a query (for
295| *   jump-on-Enter), or null when nothing matches.
296| * @example findBestMatch('git') => { id: 'git-repo', tab: 'files', … }
297| * @param {string} query - Raw user input.
298| * @returns {Object|null} The best matching entry, if any.
299| ***/
300|export const findBestMatch = (query) => searchSettings(query)[0] ?? null;

244| *   lead. A non-array `keywords` field scores 0 instead of throwing.

265| *   hits, best matches first with index order breaking ties. Blank queries

224|/***
225| * MARK: SETTINGS_SEARCH_INDEX
226| * @description Search entries with their tab name filled in from
227| *   `PROJECT_SETTINGS_TABS` (the one place tab names live), so a tab rename
228| *   updates search results instead of leaving a stale copied name behind.
229| *   An entry pointing at an unknown tab keeps a plain fallback name and is
230| *   caught by the agreement test; at runtime the jump handler also ignores
231| *   unknown tabs, so a bad entry can never switch to a blank page.
232| * @example SETTINGS_SEARCH_INDEX.find((e) => e.id === 'git-repo').tabLabel => 'Files & Repos'
233| ***/
234|export const SETTINGS_SEARCH_INDEX = SETTINGS_SEARCH_INDEX_SOURCE_ENTRIES.map((entry) => ({
235|  ...entry,
236|  tabLabel: PROJECT_SETTINGS_TABS.find((tab) => tab.id === entry.tab)?.label ?? 'Project Settings',
237|}));
238|
239|/***
240| * MARK: scoreWord
241| * @description Scores one index entry against a single normalized word: 3 for
242| *   a label prefix match, 2 for a label substring, 1 for a keyword
243| *   substring, 0 for no match. Scores rank `searchSettings` so label hits
244| *   lead. A non-array `keywords` field scores 0 instead of throwing.
245| * @example scoreWord({ label: 'Git Repository URL', keywords: ['git'] }, 'git') => 3
246| * @param {Object} entry - One `SETTINGS_SEARCH_INDEX` entry.
247| * @param {string} word - Lowercase query word.
248| * @returns {number} Match score (0 = no match).
249| ***/
250|const scoreWord = (entry, word) => {
251|  const label = String(entry?.label ?? '').toLowerCase();
252|  if (label.startsWith(word)) return 3;
253|  if (label.includes(word)) return 2;
254|  const keywords = Array.isArray(entry?.keywords) ? entry.keywords : [];
255|  if (keywords.some((keyword) => String(keyword).toLowerCase().includes(word))) return 1;
256|  return 0;
257|};
258|
259|/***
260| * MARK: searchSettings
261| * @description Returns index entries matching a query (case-insensitive).
262| *   Multi-word queries match when EVERY word hits (label substring or
263| *   keyword substring), so "centralised docs folder" finds the docs-link
264| *   setting however the words are ordered. Scores sum the per-word best
265| *   hits, best matches first with index order breaking ties. Blank queries
266| *   and non-matches return an empty array.
267| * @example searchSettings('git') => [{ id: 'git-repo', tab: 'files', … }]
268| * @param {string} query - Raw user input.
269| * @returns {Array<Object>} Matching entries, ranked best-first.
270| ***/
271|export const searchSettings = (query) => {
272|  const normalized = String(query ?? '')
273|    .trim()
274|    .toLowerCase();
275|  if (!normalized) return [];
276|  const words = normalized.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
277|  return SETTINGS_SEARCH_INDEX.map((entry, index) => {
278|    let score = 0;
279|    for (const word of words) {
280|      const wordScore = scoreWord(entry, word);
281|      // One missed word disqualifies the entry (AND semantics).
282|      if (wordScore === 0) return null;
283|      score += wordScore;
284|    }
285|    return { entry, score, index };
286|  })
287|    .filter((hit) => hit !== null)
288|    .sort((first, second) => second.score - first.score || first.index - second.index)
289|    .map((hit) => hit.entry);
290|};
291|
292|/***
293| * MARK: findBestMatch
294| * @description Returns the single best index entry for a query (for
295| *   jump-on-Enter), or null when nothing matches.
296| * @example findBestMatch('git') => { id: 'git-repo', tab: 'files', … }
297| * @param {string} query - Raw user input.
298| * @returns {Object|null} The best matching entry, if any.
299| ***/
300|export const findBestMatch = (query) => searchSettings(query)[0] ?? null;

1|# Fix verification — "Cant see settings in the Ui" (stage 4, 2026-11-20)
2|
3|## Root cause (confirmed by bundle forensics this attempt)
4|
5|The instance the human checks (`http://192.168.1.206:3100`, bundle
6|`/assets/index-Ci5jdoJ7.js`, fetched live this attempt) runs a build from
7|before this branch's visibility fixes:
8|
9|- It contains the bare label `Advanced options` ×2 (Create + Adopt) with the
10|  body rendered only under `k && (<div …>` — i.e. **closed by default**, no
11|  naming of the option — and **zero** occurrences of
12|  `Advanced options: separate docs repo` (grep count 0).
13|- It does contain the Settings → Files & Repos docs-repo input, but the
14|  Create/Import path — the one the task text calls "allowed from the
15|  default" — shows no trace of the setting until the user guesses to expand
16|  a generic "Advanced options".
17|
18|Current branch source fixes all three defects (all verified in source this
19|attempt, not just by tests):
20|
21|- `frontend/src/components/layout/Header.jsx:316,327` —
22|  `useState(true)` for both `createAdvancedOpen`/`adoptAdvancedOpen`:
23|  Advanced is **expanded by default**; the toggle is named
24|  "Advanced options: separate docs repo" (`Header.jsx:849,997`) so it stays
25|  findable even if collapsed.
26|- `Header.jsx:764,785,895,916` — dialog `max-h-[90vh]` + pinned header +
27|  scrolling form (the `SystemGuideModal` pattern): the docs field and the
28|  Create/Add buttons stay reachable on short viewports.
29|- `frontend/src/components/settings/PathsAndReposSection.jsx:202` — bordered
30|  "📚 Separate Docs Repository" block (heading + Enabled/Disabled status +
31|  URL + local-path fields) in Settings → Files & Repos; the Project tab
32|  carries the `Separate Docs Repository: On/Off` summary row with a
33|  "Manage in Files & Repos" jump (`ProjectBasicsSection.jsx:349`); the
34|  settings search index covers `separate/docs/repo/private/stealth/remote`
35|  (`projectSettingsSearch.js:174,181`).
36|
37|No further source change was needed: the defect was deployment age, not
38|code. This stage therefore re-proves visibility from current source and
39|confirms the branch is merge-ready; the setting becomes visible in
40|`192.168.1.206:3100` when the engine merges this branch and runs
41|`deploy.sh --prod` (the backend host is a different machine,
42|`192.168.1.206` ≠ this runner's `192.168.1.172`, so there is no
43|in-worktree way to push it there).
44|
45|## This attempt's evidence (all observed, not assumed)
46|
47|- Frontend tests (touched area): `npx vitest run Header / ProjectSettings /
48|  PathsAndReposSection / ProjectBasicsSection / projectSettingsSearch` —
49|  **159/159 pass**.
50|- Fresh production bundle: `npx vite build` green (4.35s); the new
51|  `frontend/dist` bundle contains `Advanced options: separate docs repo`,
52|  `Separate Docs Repository URL`, `Docs Repo Local Path`,
53|  `Separate Docs Repository:`, `Configure in Files & Repos`, and
54|  `max-h-[90vh]` (each ≥1 file in `dist/assets/`). `frontend/dist` is
55|  gitignored — deploy rebuilds it.
56|- Live UI proof from THIS branch (vite dev serving branch source + stub API
57|  with a `docsRepo`-enabled project, headless Chromium @1280×720 —
58|  realistic laptop viewport, script at `/tmp/verify-docsrepo-ui.mjs`):
59|  **11/11 DOM assertions pass**, including "Create dialog renders the docs
60|  URL field without clicking the toggle" and "field inside the 720px
61|  viewport" (y=455).
62|- Screenshots (PNG magic + `file` verified, `check:binaries` and
63|  `check:proof-hygiene` green):
64|  - `stage4-proof-1-create-720.png` — Create dialog, Advanced open, docs
65|    URL field + explainer visible, buttons reachable.
66|  - `stage4-proof-2-adopt-720-scrolled.png` — Add Existing dialog,
67|    scrolled form (scroll=697 > client=553), URL + local-path fields.
68|  - `stage4-proof-3-settings-files-repos-720.png` — Files & Repos,
69|    "Enabled … demo-kainbain-docs.git" status + both fields.
70|  - `stage4-proof-4-settings-project-jump.png` — Project tab `ON` summary
71|    + jump lands on the Files & Repos fields.
72|  - `stage4-proof-5-settings-search.png` — search `stealth` → entry jump.
73|- Branch freshness (re-fetched `origin` this attempt): **0 behind / 8
74|  ahead** of `origin/main`; `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/main`
75|  exits 0 with **zero conflict markers**. Working tree carries only this
76|  report + the 5 proof screenshots (the `/tmp` script is not part of the
77|  deliverable).
78|
79|## Where to find it after merge + deploy
80|
81|1. Create: Project dropdown → **+ New Project** → *Advanced options:
82|   separate docs repo* (already open) → `Docs Repository URL (optional)`.
83|   Collapse it only if you want it out of the way.
84|2. Import: Project dropdown → **+ Add Existing Project…** → same Advanced
85|   section → URL + `Docs Repo Local Path (optional)`. Both dialogs scroll
86|   if the window is short.
87|3. Existing project: **Settings** tab → **Files & Repos** → *📚 Separate
88|   Docs Repository* block (status line + URL + local path). The **Project**
89|   tab shows the `Separate Docs Repository: On/Off` row with a jump
90|   button; typing `separate docs repo` (or `stealth`) in settings search
91|   goes straight to the fields.

# Implementation Plan — Separate KainBain Docs Repo per Project

Task: `7f6220c3-c536-489c-b952-9858aae9ef21`
Status: planning (no code changed in this stage)
Companion survey: `./SURVEY.md` (7 questions, currently **unanswered** — see §2)

## 1. Goal and non-goals

**Goal.** Let a project store its KainBain-specific information in a *separate,
private* git repo ("docs repo") instead of inside the main project repo, so that:

- large projects are not bloated by `docs/tasks/*` history;
- teams with non-KainBain users (or public repos) see no KainBain traces;
- a solo user can "stealth use" KainBain at work on a shared repo;
- runners check out the docs repo adjacent to the main repo with synced task
  branches, keeping operations as close to normal as possible;
- the option is offered in UI configuration at project import/create time
  (especially on import).

**Explicit non-goals for v1** (to be confirmed against survey answers):

- Multi-project sharing of one docs repo (survey q7) — v1 is one docs repo per
  project; sharing is designed-for but not built.
- Automatic migration of existing docs into the new repo (survey q4) — v1
  offers "leave old docs, new work goes to the separate repo" plus a documented
  manual move; auto-move is a follow-up.
- Hiding `kb/<taskId>` working branches from the shared main repo (survey q6)

# Implementation Plan — Separate KainBain Docs Repo per Project

Task: `7f6220c3-c536-489c-b952-9858aae9ef21`
Status: planning (no code changed in this stage)
Companion survey: `./SURVEY.md` (7 questions, currently **unanswered** — see §2)

## 1. Goal and non-goals

**Goal.** Let a project store its KainBain-specific information in a *separate,
private* git repo ("docs repo") instead of inside the main project repo, so that:

- large projects are not bloated by `docs/tasks/*` history;
- teams with non-KainBain users (or public repos) see no KainBain traces;
- a solo user can "stealth use" KainBain at work on a shared repo;
- runners check out the docs repo adjacent to the main repo with synced task
  branches, keeping operations as close to normal as possible;
- the option is offered in UI configuration at project import/create time
  (especially on import).

**Explicit non-goals for v1** (to be confirmed against survey answers):

- Multi-project sharing of one docs repo (survey q7) — v1 is one docs repo per
  project; sharing is designed-for but not built.
- Automatic migration of existing docs into the new repo (survey q4) — v1
  offers "leave old docs, new work goes to the separate repo" plus a documented
  manual move; auto-move is a follow-up.
- Hiding `kb/<taskId>` working branches from the shared main repo (survey q6)
  — v1 keeps code branches in the main repo and separates only docs/state (the
  simplest reading of the task); full branch stealth is a named follow-up with
  its own design section (§7).

- `runner/project.js` — `prepareWorkdir({ repoUrl, localPath, workRoot,

### 3.4 Key invariants to preserve

1. **Single-branch resolvers**: `resolveDocsPath` / `resolveKainbainDir` stay

   hand-builds `cwd + "/docs"`.
2. **Redacted-at-rest URLs**: stored repo URLs are redacted; live git reads
   `.git/config` (see `detectGitRemote`, `redactCredentials`).
3. **Never-lose-work git hygiene**: recovery branches, no force-delete of
   unpushed work, `WORKTREE_CAP` eviction rules — the docs worktree inherits
   all of it.
4. **Runner ships standalone**: runner-side helpers cannot import backend code
   (the `resolveRunnerDocsDirName` duplication is intentional).
5. **Tolerant reads, strict writes**: resolvers degrade to defaults on garbage;

## 4. Target design (v1)

### 4.1 Data model — new project fields

```text
project.docsRepo: {
  url: string|null        # credential-REDACTED remote URL, e.g. "https://git.example.com/me/proj-kb.git"
  localPath: string|null  # backend-side checkout of the docs repo (absolute).
                          # For adopted/local setups: a path the operator gives or
                          # KainBain provisions next to cwd. For remote-backed: the
                          # backend's own clone/mirror location.
  branchMode: "synced"    # v1 fixed: docs repo carries the same kb/<taskId>
                          # branches as the code repo (see §4.3). Reserved for
                          # future "single-branch" mode.
  # auth: decided by research spike R1. Preferred: reuse the host's existing
  # credential mechanism per-remote (git credential helper / env), with an
  # optional per-project docs credential slot when R1 shows a gap.
}
```

- Absent `docsRepo` (legacy projects, default) = today's behaviour, byte for
  byte. This is the compatibility anchor: every new branch is `if
  (hasDocsRepo(project)) … else …today…`.
- Validation mirrors `assertValidDocsDirNameForWrite`:
  `assertValidDocsRepoForWrite` → 400 `INVALID_DOCS_REPO_*` codes; tolerant
  `normalizeDocsRepoSettings` for reads.
- One docs repo per project enforced (q7): backend refuses a `localPath`/`url`
  already claimed by another project (clear 409 message), until sharing is
  designed.

### 4.2 Backend layout — "KainBain home" split

Introduce one concept: **`kainbainHome/projectCwd` split**.

- Today: `projectCwd` serves as *both* code home and KainBain home
  (`<cwd>/docs/tasks`, `<cwd>/.kainbain/*`).
- With `docsRepo`: code home stays `projectCwd`; KainBain home becomes the
  docs-repo checkout (`docsRepo.localPath` on the backend).
- Implementation: add `resolveKainbainHome(project, projectCwd)` =
  `docsRepo.localPath || projectCwd`, then re-point `resolveDocsPath` and
  `resolveKainbainDir` at it (they already take `(cwd, project)` — the
  signature barely changes; internally `cwd` becomes "kainbain home").
  All downstream consumers (`taskDocsFiles`, `taskWorkspace`,
  `resolveTaskDocsDir`, `reportRelPath`, …) inherit the move with no edits —
  this is the "make change easy" payoff.
- `ensureDocsLink` / centralised-docs symlink: when `docsRepo` is set, the
  `<cwd>/docs` symlink is **not created** (stealth, q5) and
  `centralizedDocs` is ignored for that project (documented precedence:
  `docsRepo` > `centralizedDocs:false` > symlink). The docs checkout itself is
  a real git repo, not a symlink.
- `.gitignore` management: today KainBain writes ignore entries for
  `docs/tasks/` + `.kainbain/` into the main repo. With `docsRepo`, nothing is
  written into the main repo (q5 ★); equivalent ignores (if still needed) live
  in the docs repo. Audit every ignore-writing call site in Phase 1.
- `project.json`: per q1 ★, the authoritative copy lives in the docs repo
  (`<docsHome>/.kainbain/project.json`… or flattened — decided in Phase 1;
  recommend keeping the `.kainbain/` layout identical so resolvers don't fork).
  The backend's project *registry* (`projectRegistry.js`) keeps a pointer so
  `scanProjects` still finds the project. Main repo keeps zero files.

### 4.3 Branching — synced task branches across two repos

- The docs repo carries the **same branch names** as the code repo:
  `kb/<taskId>` per task, same default branch. "Synced" means: created from
  the same base event, checked out/created together at stage pickup
  (`ensureTaskBranch` gains a docs-repo twin), and pushed together at handoff.
- Merge/review semantics stay code-repo-driven: the Merge stage merges code;
  docs branches merge (or fast-forward) alongside so docs history tracks task
  history. Exact merge coupling (same commit message? docs-merge part of the
  merge stage, or lazy?) is decided in design task D3 (Phase 1) — v1 default:
  docs branch is merged/fast-forwarded by the same stage right after the code
  merge, failures reported but never blocking the code merge verdict… or
  blocking — D3 decides with a written rationale.
- Runner workdir layout becomes a pair:
  `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>` (code worktree, as today) +
  `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>-docs` (docs worktree, same branch name), each with
  its own mirror (`mirrors/<code-slug>`, `mirrors/<docs-slug>`).
  `prepareWorkdir` grows a `docsRepoUrl` option; eviction/recovery/reap logic
  treats the pair atomically (evict/reap both, park both).
- `syncTaskDocs` becomes a no-op source change: with docsRepo, task docs live
  *in* the docs worktree already — the copy step is skipped and
  `KAINBAIN_TASK_DOCS` points at the docs worktree path. `collectTaskFiles`
  reads from the docs worktree. `commitAndPush` commits+pushes **both**
  worktrees (docs first or code first — D3 decides; recommend docs-first so a
  half-pushed state never shows code without its docs… or code-first — D3
  writes the rationale either way).

### 4.4 Auth (pending spike R1 — shape, not final)

- Backend git ops and runner `runGit` both rely on ambient credentials today
  (live `.git/config` remotes + `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` fail-fast). The docs
  remote must authenticate the same way wherever possible (same host ⇒ same
  credential helper ⇒ zero new secrets UI).
- If R1 finds runners/hosts where ambient auth can't cover a second remote,
  add an optional per-project docs credential stored server-side, injected via
  `GIT_ASKPASS`/header at clone/fetch time, never persisted into `.git/config`,
  never logged (extend `redactCredentials` coverage + a redaction test).
- Hard rule: docs-repo credentials must never leak into the main repo, task
  docs, logs, or claim payloads. Spike R1 must name the exact mechanism before
  Phase 2 starts.

# Implementation Plan — Separate KainBain Docs Repo per Project

Task: `7f6220c3-c536-489c-b952-9858aae9ef21`
Status: planning (no code changed in this stage)
Companion survey: `./SURVEY.md` (7 questions, currently **unanswered** — see §2)

## 1. Goal and non-goals

**Goal.** Let a project store its KainBain-specific information in a *separate,
private* git repo ("docs repo") instead of inside the main project repo, so that:

- large projects are not bloated by `docs/tasks/*` history;
- teams with non-KainBain users (or public repos) see no KainBain traces;
- a solo user can "stealth use" KainBain at work on a shared repo;
- runners check out the docs repo adjacent to the main repo with synced task
  branches, keeping operations as close to normal as possible;
- the option is offered in UI configuration at project import/create time
  (especially on import).

**Explicit non-goals for v1** (to be confirmed against survey answers):

- Multi-project sharing of one docs repo (survey q7) — v1 is one docs repo per
  project; sharing is designed-for but not built.
- Automatic migration of existing docs into the new repo (survey q4) — v1
  offers "leave old docs, new work goes to the separate repo" plus a documented
  manual move; auto-move is a follow-up.
- Hiding `kb/<taskId>` working branches from the shared main repo (survey q6)
  — v1 keeps code branches in the main repo and separates only docs/state (the
  simplest reading of the task); full branch stealth is a named follow-up with
  its own design section (§7).

## 2. Survey analysis (SURVEY.md) — unanswered, with recommendations

The grill survey exists but `answers` is `{}` — nobody has answered yet. The
plan below assumes the **recommended** answer for each question (marked ★) and
notes where the code must keep the other option open. Before implementation
starts, re-run the grill (or get 5 minutes of the requester's time) to confirm;
each recommendation is one line to flip.

| # | Question | Recommended answer ★ | Why / plan impact |
|---|----------|----------------------|-------------------|
| q1 | What lives in the docs repo? | ★ **Everything KainBain**: task docs (`docs/tasks/*`), plans, reports, **and** KainBain settings/state (`.kainbain/` contents: `project.json`, sessions, worktrees, quarantine) | Stealth requires zero KainBain traces in the main repo (q5). Splitting settings from docs would leave a decision matrix in every resolver. One "KainBain home" location keeps `resolveDocsPath`/`resolveKainbainDir` a single-branch change. If q1 instead resolves to "task docs only", Phase 3 still works: `project.json` stays in main repo and only the docs resolvers move — the seam is the same. |
| q2 | Where in the import/create UI? | ★ **Tucked under an 'Advanced' section** on *both* create and import dialogs | Task text says "as an advance option" and "allowed from the default when you import/create". Advanced-collapsed keeps the simple form simple (existing dialogs are minimal: name+remote, path+name) while satisfying "from the default". Also add the same fields to Project Settings (Paths & Repositories) so it can be enabled later. |
| q3 | Auth for the (private) docs repo? | ★ **Separate login details just for the docs repo** (stored credential, optional: fall back to same-as-main when blank) | Main repo may be public/shared with no credential while docs repo is private, or the two live on different hosts. Design a `docsRepo` credential slot reusing the existing credential-redaction + `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` patterns; empty = "same as main repo" keeps the simple case one field. Research spike R1 (Phase 0) must confirm the current credential flow first. |
| q4 | Existing docs when switching on? | ★ **Leave old docs; only new work goes to the separate repo** (+ documented manual move command) | Auto-move is a data-loss-risky migration (symlink/shadow history — see `ensureDocsLink` incident note). Leave-in-place is safe, reversible, and matches "make change easy then make the change". Auto-move becomes a follow-up stage with its own backup/verify semantics. |
| q5 | Main repo completely free of traces? | ★ **Yes — nothing KainBain-related in the main repo** | This is the stated stealth goal ("so I can stealth use kainbain at work"). Consequences: no `.kainbain/` dir, no `docs/tasks/` content, no pointer file, and (v1) `.gitignore` entries must also not be written into the main repo — they move into the docs repo / global config. | q7 | One docs repo per project, or shared? | ★ **One docs repo per project only (v1)** | Sharing needs namespacing (`<docsRepo>/<projectSlug>/tasks/...`), cross-project locking, and quota/permission questions. Design the on-disk layout with a namespaced root anyway (`tasks/` at top level today, reservable for `<slug>/` prefix later) so sharing is additive. |

  `projects.docsSettings.test.js`, `projects.kainbainDir.test.js` show the
  established validation/test pattern to copy).

### 3.2 Runner — adjacent checkout and synced branches

- `runner/project.js` — `prepareWorkdir({ repoUrl, localPath, workRoot,
  taskId })`: clone-mode mirror at `<workRoot>/mirrors/<slug>` (+
  `refreshMirror`) or adopt-mode local path; per-task worktree
  `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>` on branch `kb/<taskId>` (+
  `refreshWorktreeToRemote`, LRU eviction under `WORKTREE_CAP`,
  `kb-recovery/*` parking). `syncTaskDocs` copies
  `<primaryCwd>/docs/tasks/<id>` into the worktree; `writeClaimTaskAssets`
  covers remote runners; `resolveRunnerDocsDirName` mirrors the backend
  resolver (deliberately duplicated — "the Runner ships without the backend
  tree"). `collectTaskFiles` in `runner/daemon.js` ships worktree files back.
- `runner/gitOps.js` — `commitAndPush` / `integrateUpstream`: stage-end handoff
  pushes the worktree (code + docs together today).
- Runner git runs with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, 60s budget, per-workdir
  serialisation, stale-lock recovery (`RunnerGitError` codes). The docs
  checkout must reuse `runGit`, not invent a second git path.
- Runner ↔ backend file transfer for task docs goes through the worktree +
  claim payloads (`taskFiles`, `taskAssets`), not through direct docs-repo
  access — this is what lets a remote runner work with no primary checkout.

### 3.3 Frontend — create/import/settings

- `frontend/src/components/layout/Header.jsx` — New Project modal (name + git
  remote) and Add Existing Project modal (path + display name + KainBain
  folder). No "Advanced" disclosure exists yet — one must be added (q2).
- `frontend/src/components/settings/PathsAndReposSection.jsx` (+
  `ProjectSettingsForm.jsx`) — Files & Repositories block: cwd, notes symlink,
  docs folder name, KainBain folder name, centralised-docs toggle, git URL,
  task-branch options. This is where the docs-repo URL + credential fields land
  for existing projects.

### 3.4 Key invariants to preserve

1. **Single-branch resolvers**: `resolveDocsPath` / `resolveKainbainDir` stay
   the only place that maps (project, cwd) → absolute path. No caller
   hand-builds `cwd + "/docs"`.
2. **Redacted-at-rest URLs**: stored repo URLs are redacted; live git reads
   `.git/config` (see `detectGitRemote`, `redactCredentials`).
3. **Never-lose-work git hygiene**: recovery branches, no force-delete of
   unpushed work, `WORKTREE_CAP` eviction rules — the docs worktree inherits
   all of it.
4. **Runner ships standalone**: runner-side helpers cannot import backend code
   (the `resolveRunnerDocsDirName` duplication is intentional).
5. **Tolerant reads, strict writes**: resolvers degrade to defaults on garbage;
   write paths 400 with `INVALID_*` codes (see `assertValidDocsDirNameForWrite`
   pattern).

## 4. Target design (v1)

### 4.1 Data model — new project fields

```text
project.docsRepo: {
  url: string|null        # credential-REDACTED remote URL, e.g. "https://git.example.com/me/proj-kb.git"
  localPath: string|null  # backend-side checkout of the docs repo (absolute).
                          # For adopted/local setups: a path the operator gives or
                          # KainBain provisions next to cwd. For remote-backed: the
                          # backend's own clone/mirror location.
  branchMode: "synced"    # v1 fixed: docs repo carries the same kb/<taskId>
                          # branches as the code repo (see §4.3). Reserved for
                          # future "single-branch" mode.
  # auth: decided by research spike R1. Preferred: reuse the host's existing
  # credential mechanism per-remote (git credential helper / env), with an
  # optional per-project docs credential slot when R1 shows a gap.
}
```

- Absent `docsRepo` (legacy projects, default) = today's behaviour, byte for
  byte. This is the compatibility anchor: every new branch is `if
  (hasDocsRepo(project)) … else …today…`.
- Validation mirrors `assertValidDocsDirNameForWrite`:
  `assertValidDocsRepoForWrite` → 400 `INVALID_DOCS_REPO_*` codes; tolerant
  `normalizeDocsRepoSettings` for reads.
- One docs repo per project enforced (q7): backend refuses a `localPath`/`url`
  already claimed by another project (clear 409 message), until sharing is
  designed.

### 4.2 Backend layout — "KainBain home" split

Introduce one concept: **`kainbainHome/projectCwd` split**.

- Today: `projectCwd` serves as *both* code home and KainBain home
  (`<cwd>/docs/tasks`, `<cwd>/.kainbain/*`).
- With `docsRepo`: code home stays `projectCwd`; KainBain home becomes the
  docs-repo checkout (`docsRepo.localPath` on the backend).
- Implementation: add `resolveKainbainHome(project, projectCwd)` =
  `docsRepo.localPath || projectCwd`, then re-point `resolveDocsPath` and
  `resolveKainbainDir` at it (they already take `(cwd, project)` — the
  signature barely changes; internally `cwd` becomes "kainbain home").
  All downstream consumers (`taskDocsFiles`, `taskWorkspace`,
  `resolveTaskDocsDir`, `reportRelPath`, …) inherit the move with no edits —
  this is the "make change easy" payoff.
- `ensureDocsLink` / centralised-docs symlink: when `docsRepo` is set, the
  `<cwd>/docs` symlink is **not created** (stealth, q5) and
  `centralizedDocs` is ignored for that project (documented precedence:
  `docsRepo` > `centralizedDocs:false` > symlink). The docs checkout itself is
  a real git repo, not a symlink.
- `.gitignore` management: today KainBain writes ignore entries for
  `docs/tasks/` + `.kainbain/` into the main repo. With `docsRepo`, nothing is
  written into the main repo (q5 ★); equivalent ignores (if still needed) live
  in the docs repo. Audit every ignore-writing call site in Phase 1.
- `project.json`: per q1 ★, the authoritative copy lives in the docs repo
  (`<docsHome>/.kainbain/project.json`… or flattened — decided in Phase 1;
  recommend keeping the `.kainbain/` layout identical so resolvers don't fork).
  The backend's project *registry* (`projectRegistry.js`) keeps a pointer so
  `scanProjects` still finds the project. Main repo keeps zero files.

### 4.3 Branching — synced task branches across two repos

- The docs repo carries the **same branch names** as the code repo:
  `kb/<taskId>` per task, same default branch. "Synced" means: created from
  the same base event, checked out/created together at stage pickup
  (`ensureTaskBranch` gains a docs-repo twin), and pushed together at handoff.
- Merge/review semantics stay code-repo-driven: the Merge stage merges code;
  docs branches merge (or fast-forward) alongside so docs history tracks task
  history. Exact merge coupling (same commit message? docs-merge part of the
  merge stage, or lazy?) is decided in design task D3 (Phase 1) — v1 default:
  docs branch is merged/fast-forwarded by the same stage right after the code
  merge, failures reported but never blocking the code merge verdict… or
  blocking — D3 decides with a written rationale.
- Runner workdir layout becomes a pair:
  `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>` (code worktree, as today) +
  `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>-docs` (docs worktree, same branch name), each with
  its own mirror (`mirrors/<code-slug>`, `mirrors/<docs-slug>`).
  `prepareWorkdir` grows a `docsRepoUrl` option; eviction/recovery/reap logic
  treats the pair atomically (evict/reap both, park both).
- `syncTaskDocs` becomes a no-op source change: with docsRepo, task docs live
  *in* the docs worktree already — the copy step is skipped and
  `KAINBAIN_TASK_DOCS` points at the docs worktree path. `collectTaskFiles`
  reads from the docs worktree. `commitAndPush` commits+pushes **both**
  worktrees (docs first or code first — D3 decides; recommend docs-first so a
  half-pushed state never shows code without its docs… or code-first — D3
  writes the rationale either way).

### 4.4 Auth (pending spike R1 — shape, not final)

- Backend git ops and runner `runGit` both rely on ambient credentials today
  (live `.git/config` remotes + `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` fail-fast). The docs
  remote must authenticate the same way wherever possible (same host ⇒ same
  credential helper ⇒ zero new secrets UI).
- If R1 finds runners/hosts where ambient auth can't cover a second remote,
  add an optional per-project docs credential stored server-side, injected via
  `GIT_ASKPASS`/header at clone/fetch time, never persisted into `.git/config`,
  never logged (extend `redactCredentials` coverage + a redaction test).
- Hard rule: docs-repo credentials must never leak into the main repo, task
  docs, logs, or claim payloads. Spike R1 must name the exact mechanism before
  Phase 2 starts.

Ordering principle: **research spikes and "make change easy" refactors first;
user-visible behaviour last; each phase is independently shippable and leaves
the tree green.** Big/risky pieces (two-repo execution model, auth) are
investigated in Phase 0 before any behaviour changes.

# Implementation Plan — Separate KainBain Docs Repo per Project

Task: `7f6220c3-c536-489c-b952-9858aae9ef21`
Status: planning (no code changed in this stage)
Companion survey: `./SURVEY.md` (7 questions, currently **unanswered** — see §2)

## 1. Goal and non-goals

**Goal.** Let a project store its KainBain-specific information in a *separate,
private* git repo ("docs repo") instead of inside the main project repo, so that:

- large projects are not bloated by `docs/tasks/*` history;
- teams with non-KainBain users (or public repos) see no KainBain traces;
- a solo user can "stealth use" KainBain at work on a shared repo;
- runners check out the docs repo adjacent to the main repo with synced task
  branches, keeping operations as close to normal as possible;
- the option is offered in UI configuration at project import/create time
  (especially on import).

**Explicit non-goals for v1** (to be confirmed against survey answers):

- Multi-project sharing of one docs repo (survey q7) — v1 is one docs repo per
  project; sharing is designed-for but not built.
- Automatic migration of existing docs into the new repo (survey q4) — v1
  offers "leave old docs, new work goes to the separate repo" plus a documented
  manual move; auto-move is a follow-up.
- Hiding `kb/<taskId>` working branches from the shared main repo (survey q6)
  — v1 keeps code branches in the main repo and separates only docs/state (the
  simplest reading of the task); full branch stealth is a named follow-up with
  its own design section (§7).

Design the on-disk layout with a namespaced root anyway (`tasks/` at top level today, reservable for `<slug>/` prefix later) so sharing is additive. |

## 3. Current-state findings (grounded in the repo)

All paths below are relative to the repo root. This is the surface the plan
must move:

### 3.1 Backend — project identity and docs location

- `api/projectStore.js` — `ProjectStore`: filesystem-backed projects. Key
  fields on the project record: `cwd` (main checkout), `notesPath`/`notesDir`,
  `docsDirName` (default `docs`), `centralizedDocs` (default true),
  `kainbainDirName` (default `.kainbain`), `gitUrl`/`repoUrl`, `useBranches`.
  `createProject` / `registerProject` provision; `ensureDocsLink` verifies the

- `api/docsPath.js` — **the docs seam**: `resolveDocsDirName`,
  `isCentralizedDocsEnabled`, `normalizeDocsSettings`,
  `assertValidDocsDirNameForWrite`, `resolveDocsPath(cwd, project)`,
  `resolveTasksDir`, `resolveTaskDocsDir`, `docsProjectFor`,
  `reportRelPath`, `docsTasksIgnorePath`. Every task-docs path flows through
  here. ★ This is where "make change easy" concentrates.
- `api/kainbainDir.js` — **the state seam**: mirrors `docsPath.js` for
  `<cwd>/.kainbain/` (`resolveKainbainDir`, `resolveProjectConfigPath`,
  `resolveSessionsDir`, `resolveWorktreesDir`, `resolveQuarantineDir`,
  `kainbainIgnorePath`). Per q1-recommended, both seams move together.
- `api/work/taskDocsFiles.js`, `api/work/taskAssets.js`,
  `api/work/taskWorkspace.js` (`repairDocsLinkAfterSwitch`,
  `resolveTaskCwd`, quarantine/worktree dirs), `api/work/taskBranches.js`
  (`kb/<taskId>` branches, worktree isolation, main/task sync helpers),
  `api/work/resolveProjectCwd.js` — all take `projectCwd` and derive docs/state
  paths from it. They must learn "docs home ≠ code home" without changing
  call signatures more than necessary.
- `api/project/gitRemote.js` — `resolveDefaultGitRemote` (template-based),
  `detectGitRemote` (reads `remote.origin.url`, **credential-redacted** via
  `redactCredentials`; git ops read the live remote from `.git/config`, never
  the stored value). The docs repo needs the same treatment: stored URL
  redacted, live URL from its own `.git/config`.
- `api/routes/projects.js` — `POST /projects` (create), `POST
  /projects/register` (adopt), `PATCH` (settings incl. docs settings —
  `projects.docsSettings.test.js`, `projects.kainbainDir.test.js` show the
  established validation/test pattern to copy).

### 3.2 Runner — adjacent checkout and synced branches

- `runner/project.js` — `prepareWorkdir({ repoUrl, localPath, workRoot,
  taskId })`: clone-mode mirror at `<workRoot>/mirrors/<slug>` (+
  `refreshMirror`) or adopt-mode local path; per-task worktree
  `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>` on branch `kb/<taskId>` (+
  `refreshWorktreeToRemote`, LRU eviction under `WORKTREE_CAP`,
  `kb-recovery/*` parking). `syncTaskDocs` copies
  `<primaryCwd>/docs/tasks/<id>` into the worktree; `writeClaimTaskAssets`
  covers remote runners; `resolveRunnerDocsDirName` mirrors the backend
  resolver (deliberately duplicated — "the Runner ships without the backend
  tree"). `collectTaskFiles` in `runner/daemon.js` ships worktree files back.
- `runner/gitOps.js` — `commitAndPush` / `integrateUpstream`: stage-end handoff
  pushes the worktree (code + docs together today).
- Runner git runs with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, 60s budget, per-workdir
  serialisation, stale-lock recovery (`RunnerGitError` codes). The docs
  checkout must reuse `runGit`, not invent a second git path.
- Runner ↔ backend file transfer for task docs goes through the worktree +
  claim payloads (`taskFiles`, `taskAssets`), not through direct docs-repo
  access — this is what lets a remote runner work with no primary checkout.

### 3.3 Frontend — create/import/settings

- `frontend/src/components/layout/Header.jsx` — New Project modal (name + git
  remote) and Add Existing Project modal (path + display name + KainBain
  folder). No "Advanced" disclosure exists yet — one must be added (q2).
- `frontend/src/components/settings/PathsAndReposSection.jsx` (+
  `ProjectSettingsForm.jsx`) — Files & Repositories block: cwd, notes symlink,
  docs folder name, KainBain folder name, centralised-docs toggle, git URL,
  task-branch options. This is where the docs-repo URL + credential fields land
  for existing projects.

### 3.4 Key invariants to preserve

1. **Single-branch resolvers**: `resolveDocsPath` / `resolveKainbainDir` stay
   the only place that maps (project, cwd) → absolute path. No caller
   hand-builds `cwd + "/docs"`.
2. **Redacted-at-rest URLs**: stored repo URLs are redacted; live git reads
   `.git/config` (see `detectGitRemote`, `redactCredentials`).
3. **Never-lose-work git hygiene**: recovery branches, no force-delete of
   unpushed work, `WORKTREE_CAP` eviction rules — the docs worktree inherits
   all of it.
4. **Runner ships standalone**: runner-side helpers cannot import backend code
   (the `resolveRunnerDocsDirName` duplication is intentional).
5. **Tolerant reads, strict writes**: resolvers degrade to defaults on garbage;
   write paths 400 with `INVALID_*` codes (see `assertValidDocsDirNameForWrite`
   pattern).

## 4. Target design (v1)

### 4.1 Data model — new project fields

```text
project.docsRepo: {
  url: string|null        # credential-REDACTED remote URL, e.g. "https://git.example.com/me/proj-kb.git"
  localPath: string|null  # backend-side checkout of the docs repo (absolute).
                          # For adopted/local setups: a path the operator gives or
                          # KainBain provisions next to cwd. For remote-backed: the
                          # backend's own clone/mirror location.
  branchMode: "synced"    # v1 fixed: docs repo carries the same kb/<taskId>
                          # branches as the code repo (see §4.3). Reserved for
                          # future "single-branch" mode.
  # auth: decided by research spike R1. Preferred: reuse the host's existing
  # credential mechanism per-remote (git credential helper / env), with an
  # optional per-project docs credential slot when R1 shows a gap.
}
```

- Absent `docsRepo` (legacy projects, default) = today's behaviour, byte for
  byte. This is the compatibility anchor: every new branch is `if
  (hasDocsRepo(project)) … else …today…`.
- Validation mirrors `assertValidDocsDirNameForWrite`:
  `assertValidDocsRepoForWrite` → 400 `INVALID_DOCS_REPO_*` codes; tolerant
  `normalizeDocsRepoSettings` for reads.
- One docs repo per project enforced (q7): backend refuses a `localPath`/`url`
  already claimed by another project (clear 409 message), until sharing is
  designed.

### 4.2 Backend layout — "KainBain home" split

Introduce one concept: **`kainbainHome/projectCwd` split**.

- Today: `projectCwd` serves as *both* code home and KainBain home
  (`<cwd>/docs/tasks`, `<cwd>/.kainbain/*`).
- With `docsRepo`: code home stays `projectCwd`; KainBain home becomes the
  docs-repo checkout (`docsRepo.localPath` on the backend).
- Implementation: add `resolveKainbainHome(project, projectCwd)` =
  `docsRepo.localPath || projectCwd`, then re-point `resolveDocsPath` and
  `resolveKainbainDir` at it (they already take `(cwd, project)` — the
  signature barely changes; internally `cwd` becomes "kainbain home").
  All downstream consumers (`taskDocsFiles`, `taskWorkspace`,
  `resolveTaskDocsDir`, `reportRelPath`, …) inherit the move with no edits —
  this is the "make change easy" payoff.
- `ensureDocsLink` / centralised-docs symlink: when `docsRepo` is set, the
  `<cwd>/docs` symlink is **not created** (stealth, q5) and
  `centralizedDocs` is ignored for that project (documented precedence:
  `docsRepo` > `centralizedDocs:false` > symlink). The docs checkout itself is
  a real git repo, not a symlink.
- `.gitignore` management: today KainBain writes ignore entries for
  `docs/tasks/` + `.kainbain/` into the main repo. With `docsRepo`, nothing is
  written into the main repo (q5 ★); equivalent ignores (if still needed) live
  in the docs repo. Audit every ignore-writing call site in Phase 1.
- `project.json`: per q1 ★, the authoritative copy lives in the docs repo
  (`<docsHome>/.kainbain/project.json`… or flattened — decided in Phase 1;
  recommend keeping the `.kainbain/` layout identical so resolvers don't fork).
  The backend's project *registry* (`projectRegistry.js`) keeps a pointer so
  `scanProjects` still finds the project. Main repo keeps zero files.

### 4.3 Branching — synced task branches across two repos

- The docs repo carries the **same branch names** as the code repo:
  `kb/<taskId>` per task, same default branch. "Synced" means: created from
  the same base event, checked out/created together at stage pickup
  (`ensureTaskBranch` gains a docs-repo twin), and pushed together at handoff.
- Merge/review semantics stay code-repo-driven: the Merge stage merges code;
  docs branches merge (or fast-forward) alongside so docs history tracks task
  history. Exact merge coupling (same commit message? docs-merge part of the
  merge stage, or lazy?) is decided in design task D3 (Phase 1) — v1 default:
  docs branch is merged/fast-forwarded by the same stage right after the code
  merge, failures reported but never blocking the code merge verdict… or
  blocking — D3 decides with a written rationale.
- Runner workdir layout becomes a pair:
  `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>` (code worktree, as today) +
  `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>-docs` (docs worktree, same branch name), each with
  its own mirror (`mirrors/<code-slug>`, `mirrors/<docs-slug>`).
  `prepareWorkdir` grows a `docsRepoUrl` option; eviction/recovery/reap logic
  treats the pair atomically (evict/reap both, park both).
- `syncTaskDocs` becomes a no-op source change: with docsRepo, task docs live
  *in* the docs worktree already — the copy step is skipped and
  `KAINBAIN_TASK_DOCS` points at the docs worktree path. `collectTaskFiles`
  reads from the docs worktree. `commitAndPush` commits+pushes **both**
  worktrees (docs first or code first — D3 decides; recommend docs-first so a
  half-pushed state never shows code without its docs… or code-first — D3
  writes the rationale either way).

### 4.4 Auth (pending spike R1 — shape, not final)

- Backend git ops and runner `runGit` both rely on ambient credentials today
  (live `.git/config` remotes + `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` fail-fast). The docs
  remote must authenticate the same way wherever possible (same host ⇒ same
  credential helper ⇒ zero new secrets UI).
- If R1 finds runners/hosts where ambient auth can't cover a second remote,
  add an optional per-project docs credential stored server-side, injected via
  `GIT_ASKPASS`/header at clone/fetch time, never persisted into `.git/config`,
  never logged (extend `redactCredentials` coverage + a redaction test).
- Hard rule: docs-repo credentials must never leak into the main repo, task
  docs, logs, or claim payloads. Spike R1 must name the exact mechanism before
  Phase 2 starts.

# Implementation Plan — Separate KainBain Docs Repo per Project

Task: `7f6220c3-c536-489c-b952-9858aae9ef21`
Status: planning (no code changed in this stage)
Companion survey: `./SURVEY.md` (7 questions, currently **unanswered** — see §2)

## 1. Goal and non-goals

**Goal.** Let a project store its KainBain-specific information in a *separate,
private* git repo ("docs repo") instead of inside the main project repo, so that:

- large projects are not bloated by `docs/tasks/*` history;
- teams with non-KainBain users (or public repos) see no KainBain traces;
- a solo user can "stealth use" KainBain at work on a shared repo;
- runners check out the docs repo adjacent to the main repo with synced task
  branches, keeping operations as close to normal as possible;
- the option is offered in UI configuration at project import/create time
  (especially on import).

**Explicit non-goals for v1** (to be confirmed against survey answers):

- Multi-project sharing of one docs repo (survey q7) — v1 is one docs repo per
  project; sharing is designed-for but not built.
- Automatic migration of existing docs into the new repo (survey q4) — v1
  offers "leave old docs, new work goes to the separate repo" plus a documented
  manual move; auto-move is a follow-up.
- Hiding `kb/<taskId>` working branches from the shared main repo (survey q6)
  — v1 keeps code branches in the main repo and separates only docs/state (the
  simplest reading of the task); full branch stealth is a named follow-up with
  its own design section (§7).

## 2. Survey analysis (SURVEY.md) — unanswered, with recommendations

## 3. Current-state findings (grounded in the repo)

All paths below are relative to the repo root. This is the surface the plan
must move:

### 3.1 Backend — project identity and docs location

- `api/projectStore.js` — `ProjectStore`: filesystem-backed projects. Key

  `docsDirName` (default `docs`), `centralizedDocs` (default true),
  `kainbainDirName` (default `.kainbain`), `gitUrl`/`repoUrl`, `useBranches`.
  `createProject` / `registerProject` provision; `ensureDocsLink` verifies the
  `<cwd>/<docsDir>/ → notes-space` symlink with careful repair policy.
- `api/docsPath.js` — **the docs seam**: `resolveDocsDirName`,
  `isCentralizedDocsEnabled`, `normalizeDocsSettings`,
  `assertValidDocsDirNameForWrite`, `resolveDocsPath(cwd, project)`,
  `resolveTasksDir`, `resolveTaskDocsDir`, `docsProjectFor`,
  `reportRelPath`, `docsTasksIgnorePath`. Every task-docs path flows through
  here. ★ This is where "make change easy" concentrates.
- `api/kainbainDir.js` — **the state seam**: mirrors `docsPath.js` for
  `<cwd>/.kainbain/` (`resolveKainbainDir`, `resolveProjectConfigPath`,
  `resolveSessionsDir`, `resolveWorktreesDir`, `resolveQuarantineDir`,
  `kainbainIgnorePath`). Per q1-recommended, both seams move together.
- `api/work/taskDocsFiles.js`, `api/work/taskAssets.js`,
  `api/work/taskWorkspace.js` (`repairDocsLinkAfterSwitch`,
  `resolveTaskCwd`, quarantine/worktree dirs), `api/work/taskBranches.js`
  (`kb/<taskId>` branches, worktree isolation, main/task sync helpers),
  `api/work/resolveProjectCwd.js` — all take `projectCwd` and derive docs/state
  paths from it. They must learn "docs home ≠ code home" without changing
  call signatures more than necessary.
- `api/project/gitRemote.js` — `resolveDefaultGitRemote` (template-based),
  `detectGitRemote` (reads `remote.origin.url`, **credential-redacted** via
  `redactCredentials`; git ops read the live remote from `.git/config`, never

  redacted, live URL from its own `.git/config`.
- `api/routes/projects.js` — `POST /projects` (create), `POST
  /projects/register` (adopt), `PATCH` (settings incl. docs settings —
  `projects.docsSettings.test.js`, `projects.kainbainDir.test.js` show the
  established validation/test pattern to copy).

### 3.2 Runner — adjacent checkout and synced branches

- `runner/project.js` — `prepareWorkdir({ repoUrl, localPath, workRoot,
  taskId })`: clone-mode mirror at `<workRoot>/mirrors/<slug>` (+
  `refreshMirror`) or adopt-mode local path; per-task worktree
  `<workRoot>/kb-<taskId>` on branch `kb/<taskId>` (+
  `refreshWorktreeToRemote`, LRU eviction under `WORKTREE_CAP`,
  `kb-recovery/*` parking). `syncTaskDocs` copies
  `<primaryCwd>/docs/tasks/<id>` into the worktree; `writeClaimTaskAssets`
  covers remote runners; `resolveRunnerDocsDirName` mirrors the backend
  resolver (deliberately duplicated — "the Runner ships without the backend
  tree"). `collectTaskFiles` in `runner/daemon.js` ships worktree files back.
- `runner/gitOps.js` — `commitAndPush` / `integrateUpstream`: stage-end handoff
  pushes the worktree (code + docs together today).
- Runner git runs with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, 60s budget, per-workdir
  serialisation, stale-lock recovery (`RunnerGitError` codes). The docs
  checkout must reuse `runGit`, not invent a second git path.
- Runner ↔ backend file transfer for task docs goes through the worktree +
  claim payloads (`taskFiles`, `taskAssets`), not through direct docs-repo
  access — this is what lets a remote runner work with no primary checkout.

### 3.3 Frontend — create/import/settings

- `frontend/src/components/layout/Header.jsx` — New Project modal (name + git
  remote) and Add Existing Project modal (path + display name + KainBain
  folder). No "Advanced" disclosure exists yet — one must be added (q2).
- `frontend/src/components/settings/PathsAndReposSection.jsx` (+
  `ProjectSettingsForm.jsx`) — Files & Repositories block: cwd, notes symlink,
  docs folder name, KainBain folder name, centralised-docs toggle, git URL,
  task-branch options. This is where the docs-repo URL + credential fields land
  for existing projects.

### 3.4 Key invariants to preserve

1. **Single-branch resolvers**: `resolveDocsPath` / `resolveKainbainDir` stay
   the only place that maps (project, cwd) → absolute path. No caller
   hand-builds `cwd + "/docs"`.
2. **Redacted-at-rest URLs**: stored repo URLs are redacted; live git reads
   `.git/config` (see `detectGitRemote`, `redactCredentials`).
3. **Never-lose-work git hygiene**: recovery branches, no force-delete of
   unpushed work, `WORKTREE_CAP` eviction rules — the docs worktree inherits
   all of it.
4. **Runner ships standalone**: runner-side helpers cannot import backend code
   (the `resolveRunnerDocsDirName` duplication is intentional).
5. **Tolerant reads, strict writes**: resolvers degrade to defaults on garbage;
   write paths 400 with `INVALID_*` codes (see `assertValidDocsDirNameForWrite`
